title: When Did OU's Boomer and Sooner Mascots Debut? The 2005 Big Red Rally
question: When were the Boomer and Sooner costumed mascots introduced at Oklahoma?
answer: OU's costumed mascots Boomer and Sooner were introduced at the Big Red Rally on campus on August 26, 2005, after nearly three years of development. They are named for the real ponies that pull the Sooner Schooner.
summary: Boomer and Sooner, OU's costumed mascots, debuted at the Big Red Rally on Aug. 26, 2005. Learn how they connect to the real Sooner Schooner ponies.
body: Oklahoma has two sets of Boomer and Sooner. One pair is real: the white ponies that pull the Sooner Schooner across Owen Field after every score. The other pair is costumed, and they made their debut at the Big Red Rally on campus on August 26, 2005.

The costumed characters were a deliberate project rather than an overnight idea. The athletics department and student leaders saw the need for a mascot that could represent OU at every athletic contest and also attend charity events and visit children's hospitals, places a wagon and ponies cannot easily go. Student congress passed a resolution supporting a unified mascot, a Mascot Committee went to work, and the process took nearly three years before Boomer and Sooner were unveiled.

The idea was to extend the Schooner rather than replace it. The costumed mascots are designed as a fan-friendly version of the wagon's ponies, especially for kids, and they appear across OU athletics. The names themselves come from the Land Run era, when Boomers campaigned to open the territory and Sooners slipped in ahead of the legal start.

The live ponies have their own lineage. The originals in 1964 were Shetland ponies, and today's Boomer and Sooner are Welsh ponies, slightly taller and heavier. Between the ponies, the costumes and the wagon, Oklahoma's mascot family manages to honor the same 1889 story in three different ways.
